desk_read: Yesterday's session was dominated by broad long liquidation across equities and metals, with S&P 500 down -3.64% on volume 1.3x its 20-day average and total open interest down -2.4k contracts (-0.1%), alongside Nasdaq 100 dropping -5.54% on volume 1.2x its 20-day average with total open interest down -1.1k contracts (-0.4%). Gold also suffered long liquidation, falling -4.62% on volume 1.1x its 20-day average as total open interest dropped -2.6k contracts (-0.7%). In contrast, silver saw new shorts as price dropped -7.41% on volume 1.3x its 20-day average while total open interest rose +240 contracts (+0.2%), making its positioning more fragile. Meanwhile, energy markets experienced short covering with WTI Crude Oil up +1.18% on volume 0.9x its 20-day average and total open interest down -1.9k contracts (-0.2%) under backwardation.
oil_read: Yesterday, WTI rose +1.18% alongside a total open interest reduction of -1.9k contracts (-0.2%), while volume printed 0.9x its 20-day average, signaling short covering amid a backwardated curve where the CLZ26-CLK27 spread stood at +5.28 $/bbl. Brent (NYMEX) similarly gained +0.57% with total open interest dropping -155 contracts (-0.1%) and volume at 0.7x its 20-day average, also reflecting short covering within a backwardated structure defined by the BZF27-BZM27 spread at +9.52 $/bbl.
bias_read: WTI Crude Oil and Brent (NYMEX) both show a mildly bullish bias driven by short covering, but because positions are closing this is less durable and warns of exhaustion rather than a durable trend. S&P 500 displays a mildly bearish bias from long liquidation with volume 1.3x the 20-day average, warning of a squeeze as longs exit. Overall, the short-term flow reflects cautious repositioning and profit-taking across asset classes rather than strong directional commitment.
